sections.heading: Section 1: Augmented Matrices and Row Echelon Form (REF)

questions.q: Which matrix represents a valid Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF)?
questions.answer: In RREF, each leading entry (pivot) is 1, is the only non-zero entry in its column, and appears to the right of pivots in previous rows, with zero rows at the bottom.

questions.q: How many pivots does a $3 \times 5$ matrix have at most?
questions.answer: Because each pivot must reside in a distinct row and a distinct column, the maximum number of pivots is $\min(m, n) = \min(3, 5) = 3$.

questions.q: An augmented matrix has a row of the form $[0, 0, \dots, 0 \mid b]$ with $b \neq 0$. What does this establish about the linear system?
choices: The system is inconsistent (has no solution)
The system has a unique solution
The system has infinitely many solutions
questions.answer: The row represents the contradictory equation $0 = b$. Any system with such a pivot in the augmented column is inconsistent.

sections.heading: Section 2: Solution Sets and Free Variables

questions.q: A consistent system has $5$ variables and $3$ pivot columns in its coefficient matrix. How many free variables does the system have?
questions.answer: The number of free variables equals total variables minus pivot columns: $5 - 3 = 2$ free variables, yielding a 2-dimensional plane of solutions.

questions.q: When does a linear system $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ possess a unique solution?
choices: When the system is consistent and every column of $A$ contains a pivot (no free variables)
Whenever the number of equations equals the number of variables
When there is at least one free variable
questions.answer: A consistent system has a unique solution if and only if every variable is a basic variable, meaning there are zero free variables.

questions.q: If a system is consistent and has at least one free variable, how many solutions exist over $\mathbb{R}$?
choices: Finite number equal to the number of free variables
questions.answer: Because free variables can take any real value, any consistent system with at least one free variable has infinitely many solutions.

sections.heading: Section 3: Homogeneous Systems and Null Space

questions.q: What is always true about the homogeneous linear system $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$?
choices: It is always consistent, because $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ is always a solution (the trivial solution)
It always has infinitely many solutions
It only has solutions when $A$ is square
questions.answer: Setting all variables to zero ($x_1 = \dots = x_n = 0$) always satisfies $A \mathbf{0} = \mathbf{0}$, so homogeneous systems are never inconsistent.

questions.q: Under what condition does the homogeneous system $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ have non-trivial solutions (solutions where $\mathbf{x} \neq \mathbf{0}$)?
choices: If and only if the system has at least one free variable
If and only if $A$ has more rows than columns
If and only if all entries of $A$ are positive
questions.answer: Non-trivial solutions exist if and only if there is at least one free variable (i.e. the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent).

questions.q: The set of all solutions to $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ forms a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$ called the:
questions.answer: By definition, $\text{Null}(A) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n : A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}\}$ is the null space of the matrix.

questions.q: According to the Invertible Matrix Theorem, for a square $n \times n$ matrix $A$, which statement is equivalent to $A$ being invertible?
choices: The equation $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ has a unique solution for each $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^n$
The columns of $A$ are linearly dependent
The null space of $A$ contains non-zero vectors
questions.answer: Invertibility is equivalent to $A$ having $n$ pivots, meaning $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ has a unique solution $\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$ for any $\mathbf{b}$.

questions.q: If $A$ is invertible and $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, how is the unique solution expressed algebraically?
questions.answer: Multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$: $A^{-1}(A \mathbf{x}) = A^{-1}\mathbf{b} \Rightarrow I \mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\mathbf{b} \Rightarrow \mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.

questions.q: If $A$ is a $4 \times 4$ matrix with rank $3$, how many solutions does $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ have?
questions.answer: By the Rank-Nullity Theorem, $\text{nullity}(A) = n - \text{rank}(A) = 4 - 3 = 1$. With a 1-dimensional null space, there are infinitely many solutions.
